findings.detail: The `@param tier Defaults to 'fast'. Web Scraper asks for 'quality'; OCR's text path deliberately does not…` block at 459-465 documented `extractStructuredData`. The new constant and its own doc comment were inserted directly after it, so that block now attaches to `export const MAX_EXTRACTION_TEXT` — a number that has no `tier` parameter. The tier rationale is load-bearing (it explains why OCR's new spreadsheet/Word path stays on 'fast'), and it is now invisible on hover at the call site in OcrTab.tsx:466.
findings.summary: MAX_EXTRACTION_TEXT was inserted between extractStructuredData and its JSDoc

findings.detail: `mapDataToTemplate([stripped], varMapping, varHeaders)[0]` (577-578) invokes `mapRowsToTemplate` per row. That function recomputes `isRewaaTemplate(templateHeaders)` — which builds `new Set(templateHeaders.map(normalizeHeader))` over the full ~70-column Rewaa template — and `headerFor(templateHeaders, 'variant name')` on every call (utils/templateMapping.ts:208-209). Previously both ran once for the whole array. It is a constant-factor regression, not a complexity change, so a few-hundred-row extraction is still fine; it would become a real problem only if this export path is ever pointed at a multi-thousand-row source, which is why it is `low` and not `medium`.
findings.summary: exportData now calls mapDataToTemplate once per row instead of once per batch

findings.detail: `wb: any` (582), `toExportRow: (row: any[]) => any[]` (584) and `issueData: any[][]` (595) are newly added lines, not reindented legacy. `wb` is always an XLSX workbook and the two call sites (695, 870) always pass the same shape, so the compiler currently cannot catch a mis-ordered argument — e.g. swapping `exportHeaders` and `issueGroups` would type-check. The handbook's escape-hatch rule is exactly about new code like this.
findings.summary: New appendIssueSheets helper introduces unjustified `any` in its signature
